<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **52** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/automation/schedule-organization.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/automation/time-relative-trigger.zod.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via time_relative (literal, a string literal in validateFlowTriggerReadiness))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via AUTHORING_RULES (symbol, a top-level const object))_
- `content/docs/permissions/capabilities.mdx`  _(via time_relative (literal, a string literal in validateFlowTriggerReadiness))_
- `content/docs/ui/reports.mdx`  _(via maxRecords (literal, a string literal in validateFlowTriggerReadiness))_
- `content/docs/ui/views.mdx`  _(via maxRecords (literal, a string literal in validateFlowTriggerReadiness))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via maxRecords (literal, a string literal in validateFlowTriggerReadiness), time_relative (literal, a string literal in validateFlowTriggerReadiness))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via time_relative (literal, a string literal in validateFlowTriggerReadiness))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/automation/schedule-organization.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/automation/time-relative-trigger.zod.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a49be31f805185410e9efdb4b0be6570a151bca` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `115451141b33ce15f2aa30376d6a7a96413e6243` — the merge of head `4466c0cc8b649939618bc6634ac946d5bccb74c8` into base `0a49be31f805185410e9efdb4b0be6570a151bca`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 115451141b33ce15f2aa30376d6a7a96413e6243 && git checkout 115451141b33ce15f2aa30376d6a7a96413e6243
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0a49be31f805185410e9efdb4b0be6570a151bca 4466c0cc8b649939618bc6634ac946d5bccb74c8 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0a49be31f805185410e9efdb4b0be6570a151bca && git merge --no-ff 4466c0cc8b649939618bc6634ac946d5bccb74c8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0a49be31f805185410e9efdb4b0be6570a151bca
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0a49be31f805185410e9efdb4b0be6570a151bca` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ee53786b52ae178bf9ea949a16c838f220a7550f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: the full diff of PR #36691 against merge base `9348f02b9052c89011893c5a10be86d5888fc0c4` (17 files: `.changeset/35143-flow-publish-checks-second-batch.md`, `packages/lint/src/{authoring-rules,flow-select-options,index,lint-flow-patterns,rule-explanations,validate-flow-node-writes,validate-flow-trigger-readiness}.ts`, the two lint test files, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.publish-refuses-flows-that-save-and-do-not-run.ts`, two example flows, four docs pages); card #35143 body and comments (premise table 7098105309, report 7100228457); PR #35244 body and its changeset (the #34776 precedent) + cited at the PR head: `packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin-extension-api.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/{crud-nodes,value-slot-map,subflow-node,map-node}.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-hooks-and-functions.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts`, `packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts`, `packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/src/{schedule-trigger,time-relative-trigger}.ts`, `packages/spec/src/automation/{flow-trigger-kind,record-change-trigger-events,time-relative-trigger.zod,schedule-organization.zod}.ts`, `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/README.md`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`, `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/execution-duties.md`, the pending `.changeset/*.md` set
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments

Each check was read against the code that runs flows. Nine of the ten hold as written. One refuses valid metadata.

- `flow-trigger-object-missing` (error): TRUE for an absent `objectName`. The binding passes `object: undefined` (`plugin-extension-api.ts:254`). The trigger hands it to `registerHook` (`record-change-trigger.ts:372-373`). `hookMatchesObject` reads an absent target as global (`engine-top-level.ts:3733-3746`). The flow starts on every object's write. The card's "binds to nothing" was corrected, and the correction is right.
- `flow-condition-option-label` (error): the premise is TRUE (the row holds the option value). **The detection is not.** See must-fix M2.
- `flow-time-relative-shadowed` (error): TRUE. `resolveFlowTriggerKind` answers `record_change` before `time_relative` (`flow-trigger-kind.ts:76-81`). The lint uses the same `startsWith('record-')` test.
- `flow-time-relative-key-misplaced` (error): TRUE. The sweep reads `desc.filter` and `desc.maxRecords` from the descriptor only (`time-relative-trigger.ts:237`, `:488`). The binding lifts only `schedule`, `organization` and `condition` (`plugin-extension-api.ts:271-293`).
- `flow-time-relative-date-field-invalid` (error): TRUE against the published contract. The sweep is a `$gte`/`$lte` range on `desc.dateField` (`time-relative-trigger.ts:238`). The schema describes the key as a "Date or datetime field" (`time-relative-trigger.zod.ts:146-149`). An unknown type is not judged. `created_at` / `updated_at` are read from the injected columns.
- `flow-schedule-timezone-missing` (warning): TRUE. `new Cron(expression, { timezone: schedule.timezone ?? 'UTC' })` (`schedule-trigger.ts:251`). `cronWithoutZone` mirrors `normalizeSchedule` (`schedule-trigger.ts:608-631`) shape for shape.
- `flow-subflow-unknown` (warning, CLI only): TRUE. A missing child fails the step (`subflow-node.ts:175`, `map-node.ts:262-284`). The CLI-only placement is forced: a flow write is handed no `flows` collection (`protocol-authoring-gate.ts:566-574`, ruling #32666).
- `flow-node-write-unknown-option` (error): TRUE. A bare string in `fields` is a literal (`value-slot-map.ts:44-56`; the single-brace template dialect is refused elsewhere). The validator refuses an off-list value with `invalid_option`, single and multi (`record-validator.ts:1892-1905`, `:1939-1950`). The lint skips what the validator skips: a `picklist` field, a `readonly` field (`:1891`), an empty options list. `String(value)` matches the validator's own reading (`:598-603`).
- `flow-node-write-date-helper-text` (error): TRUE. The string is written as text and refused `invalid_date` (`record-validator.ts:1807-1810`). The hinted helpers exist (`formula/src/stdlib.ts`, `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx:288-290`).
- `flow-create-update-pair` (warning): TRUE as an advisory. `record-after-write` binds both events (`record-change-trigger-events.ts:39`). It runs inside `lintFlowPatterns`, so the runtime gate (one flow per write) never raises it.

Example edits: not a loosened rule. The three cron schedules in `app-todo` and `app-showcase` raised only the new timezone warning. `timezone: 'UTC'` states what the runtime already did. No run-time behaviour changes. The showcase `connectorConfig` false positive was fixed in the rule (the signature now covers the whole node), not by editing the example.

**Clause-② line: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is correct. Keep it.** The repo's test is "does the card widen an accept set or enlarge the public surface" (`execution-duties.md:76-77`). The PR narrows the publish accept set (seven refusals). It also adds eleven exports to the built entry of `@objectstack/lint` (`index.ts`: `validateFlowSubflowTargets` and ten rule ids). New exports are a widening in this repo's practice (pending changesets 34779, 35113, 35892 declare `yes (widening)` for exports alone). `clause2-line.mjs` names `yes (narrowing)` as the spelling for "widens one surface and narrows another". `no (narrowing)` would be right only if the exports were not added. The #34776 changeset wrote `no (narrowing: ...)` while adding exports; that precedent under-declared the widening and should not be copied.

**Metadata-protocol line: `none` is wrong. It must read `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`.** See must-fix M1.

**must-fix M1 — `Metadata-protocol: none` and the `patch` levels.** The repo defines `narrowed` as "a key removed or tombstoned, a value refused, a requirement tightened" and grades it `minor` (`pr-automation.yml:775-778`; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs:907-910`). This PR refuses values an author could publish yesterday (a select literal, helper text, `filter` beside `timeRelative`) and tightens a requirement (`objectName` on a record trigger). The gate cannot see this class: "a refused value ... is invisible to them, so the declaration — not the diff — is still the carrier" (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs:928-932`). So `none` passes CI and is still wrong. Every pending narrowing that registers an ADR-0087 entry declares `narrowed` with `@objectstack/lint: minor`: 34776 (the first batch), 34987, 35040, 36167, 35252. This PR is the only outlier. Fix, in the PR body and the changeset both: `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, and `'@objectstack/lint': minor`. `@objectstack/spec` may stay `patch` (one moved package at `minor` discharges the rule). The `(narrowing)` arm that `narrowed` requires is already there.

**must-fix M2 — `flow-condition-option-label` refuses valid conditions, and its hint breaks them.** `optionLabelComparisons` (`flow-select-options.ts:113-125`) does not check that the label literal is compared with the select field. It checks three unrelated facts: the field is read somewhere, the label is quoted somewhere, the value is quoted nowhere. Two valid conditions it refuses, with the PR's own test object `deal`:
  - `record.stage == 'open' && record.name == 'Closed Lost'`. `stage` is read. `'Closed Lost'` is quoted, as the comparand of the text field `name`. `'closed_lost'` is absent. The rule raises an error and tells the author to write `'closed_lost'` in place of `'Closed Lost'`, which would break a working condition.
  - Two select fields where one's label is the other's value: `priority` with `{ value: 'high', label: 'High' }` and `severity` with bare options `['High', 'Low']`. `record.severity == 'High' && record.priority != null` is refused.
  The silent pin at test line 140-149 passes only because that fixture also quotes `'closed_lost'`. Fix: report only when the label literal is the comparand of that field (`F == 'L'`, `F != 'L'`, `'L' == F`, `F in [...]`), and pin both cases above as silent. Lowering the rule to a warning is the smaller alternative, but the wrong hint would remain.

**should-fix S1 — the blank-name arm of `flow-trigger-object-missing` states the wrong consequence.** For `objectName: ''` or `'  '` the trigger passes the string through, and `registerHook` throws on an empty target (`engine-hooks-and-functions.ts:236`, `engine-top-level.ts:3859-3875`). That flow is not bound. It does not "watch every object". The refusal is right; the sentence is not. Give the blank case its own message (the test at line 94 pins "the same way").

Notes:
- `flow-time-relative-date-field-invalid` treats every non-date type as "never falls in". A `summary` field that rolls up `min`/`max` of a date is outside the schema's stated contract, so the refusal stands; say so in the explanation if the lane wants.
- `flow-trigger-object-missing` also fires for an unmappable `record-*` token, where the flow is not bound at all. Rule 1c already refuses that flow.
- `DATE_HELPER_CALL` is case sensitive; `'TODAY()'` text is missed. A miss, not a false positive.

### ② Semver level

- The `!` in the title is allowed. `major` is absent, so `check-changeset-no-major` passes. The level itself is wrong: see M1 (`@objectstack/lint` must be `minor` under `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`).
- The changeset carries the `**BREAKING**` banner, a `## FROM → TO` section with six worked pairs, and the marker `adr-0087: registered publish-refuses-flows-that-save-and-do-not-run`. That satisfies `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`.
- The ADR-0087 entry is well-formed: `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`, the `SemanticMigration` type. The file name is `18.` (the protocol major, shared by 569 entries on main) plus the id, as `entries/README.md` requires. The id is unique. It mirrors the first batch's `18.publish-refuses-metadata-the-runtime-ignores.ts`. "Notice only, no D2 conversion" is right: each fix is the author's choice.
- The entry and the changeset spell no call of a live method in a way I could match to a textual ratchet; CI was still running at review time.

### ③ Boundary flags

- A published app can fail its next publish. The changeset and the entry both say so, and say that stored flows are not rewritten or refused at boot. Called out correctly.
- Shipped stacks: the PR reports `objectstack validate` clean on app-crm, app-todo and app-showcase. By reading, every record-triggered flow under `examples/`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/fixtures/` and the CLI scaffold (`packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts:652-655`) names its `objectName`. `packages/qa/dogfood/test/fixtures/schedule-organization-fixture.ts:74` keeps a cron with no timezone; that is a warning only.
- **should-fix S2 — the docs and the spec's own examples still teach the shape the new warning reports.** `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx:3097` (and the comment at `:3032`), the docblock examples at `packages/spec/src/automation/time-relative-trigger.zod.ts:44` and `schedule-organization.zod.ts:122` (the source of `content/docs/references/automation/time-relative-trigger.mdx:45` and `schedule-organization.mdx:125`) write `{ type: 'cron', expression: '0 8 * * *' }` with no `timezone`. A reader who copies them gets a warning, and `os validate --strict` exits 1. Add `timezone` there in this PR. `skills/objectstack-automation/references/integration-recipes.md:47` has the same shape; add it to the `Skills-docs:` follow-up list, which does not name it.
- No docs page names any of the seven new error ids. The first batch documented its rules in `content/docs/`. This can ride the S2 edit.
- Rule explanations: accurate for nine ids. `flow-condition-option-label` describes the co-occurrence test honestly, which is the defect in M2; it changes with the fix. `flow-trigger-object-missing` needs the blank-name sentence from S1.
- `validate-flow-trigger-readiness.test.ts`: not weakened. Four fixtures gained `timezone: 'UTC'` so their `toEqual([])` assertions keep judging their own question. No assertion was removed or loosened. One fixture moved from the bare-string cron to the object form; the bare-string shape is pinned in the new test file ("in both spellings").
- The pins fail without the fix: the new test file imports the ten new rule ids and asserts each id at the function and, for the seven errors, at `runRuntimeAuthoringRules`. `flow-time-relative-shadowed`, `-key-misplaced` and `-date-field-invalid` have function pins and no runtime-gate pin; they run inside the gate-registered `validateFlowTriggerReadiness`, so this is a note.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` still needs its card number (an L1 item).
- CI check-runs were in progress on this head at review time.

### ④ Design judgment

Against card #35143, Flows family only.

- The split is sound: seven errors where the start node or one literal settles the answer, three warnings where intent or another package may decide. Extending `validateFlowTriggerReadiness`, `validateFlowNodeWrites` and `lintFlowPatterns` follows the card's "extend it; do not add a second rule beside it". One shared options reader (`flow-select-options.ts`) for the two option rules is the right shape.
- F3 not built: accepted. The re-entry guard is on main (`service-automation/src/engine.ts:3208`). F4c and F7b are covered by existing rules.
- F6 departs from the card twice: the card marks it as a rule for the gate and the CLI, and not as advisory. The PR ships a CLI-only warning. The reason holds (the gate's flow snapshot holds only the written flow). The hosted copy of this check cannot be deleted on the strength of this PR. Record that on the card as an open line.
- F1 is covered for start conditions and CRUD writes only. Decision-node and edge conditions are not judged. The PR says so; the card needs the line, since its "done when" asks for a rule or a covering rule per line.
- The label rule's method (text co-occurrence) is the one design choice that does not hold at error tier. See M2.
- The timezone warning also fires on sub-hourly crons (`*/5 * * * *`), where the zone changes nothing. A note for the lane; skipping crons with a wildcard hour would cut the noise.

Open: must-fix M1, must-fix M2, should-fix S1, should-fix S2.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-jju3py`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JQwxbZeHNsF3RWcWpj7rGj`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `72fe0c0764df3ae49d06ded9b5da20f286a64134`
Local-runs: none
Scope: delta `ee53786b52ae178bf9ea949a16c838f220a7550f..72fe0c0764df3ae49d06ded9b5da20f286a64134` (one commit, 10 files: `.changeset/35143-flow-publish-checks-second-batch.md`, `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`, `content/docs/references/automation/{schedule-organization,time-relative-trigger}.mdx`, `packages/lint/src/{flow-select-options,rule-explanations,validate-flow-trigger-readiness}.ts`, `packages/lint/src/flow-publish-checks-second-batch.test.ts`, `packages/spec/src/automation/{schedule-organization,time-relative-trigger}.zod.ts`); the PR body at the new head; rework record 7100465508 as relayed by the seat + cited: `packages/objectql/src/engine-hooks-and-functions.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.publish-refuses-flows-that-save-and-do-not-run.ts`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml`. The first review of head `ee53786b52ae178bf9ea949a16c838f220a7550f` stands for everything the delta does not touch.
Security-touching: no
Rule-change-verified: none

### ① Derived judgments

- **M1 closed.** The PR body and the changeset both read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. The pair is consistent: `narrowed` needs the `(narrowing)` arm, and it is there.
- **M2 closed.** `optionLabelComparisons` (`flow-select-options.ts:97-154`) now reports a label only when it is the comparand of that field. Read case by case:
  - Reported, correctly: `record.stage == 'L'`, `stage != "L"`, `'L' == record.stage`, `previous.stage in ['open', 'L']`, with any whitespace or line break around the operator, inside parentheses, and inside `&&` / `||` chains.
  - `!(record.stage == 'L')` is reported. That is right: the inner comparison is false on every row, so the negation is true on every row.
  - Silent, correctly: `record.stage == 'open' && record.name == 'L'`; the two-select case (`record.severity == 'High' && record.priority != null`); a path through another object (`record.account.stage == 'L'`, `vars.stage == 'L'`); a longer field name (`other_stage`, `stage_label`); a member read (`record.stage.label`); `label(record.stage) == 'L'`.
  - Both first-review cases are pinned silent, and the mixed-case pair is pinned in both directions (test lines 164-189). The literal-first and `in`-list spellings have positive pins (lines 154-162).
  - No new false positive found. The literal-first pattern has no left boundary, so a span between two other literals can be read as a literal, but it would have to spell a label exactly and be followed by `== F`. Not a real case.
- **S1 closed.** A blank `objectName` now says "never bound and the flow never starts". That matches the engine: `registerHook` throws on an empty target (`engine-hooks-and-functions.ts:236`, `engine-top-level.ts:3859-3875`). An absent name keeps the "every object" sentence. The test pins both sentences apart. The explanation and the changeset carry the same split.

Notes:
- The old hedge "the option's value is quoted too" is gone. `record.stage == 'closed_lost' || record.stage == 'Closed Lost'` is now refused. The second arm is dead, so the refusal is defensible, but that flow did run as meant. The lane may want a line on it in the explanation.
- Misses, by design: `record["stage"]`, `'L' in [record.stage]`, a parenthesised literal, `.contains(...)`, a label that holds a quote. None refuses valid metadata.
- Not pinned: parentheses, negation, a double-quoted list member. The pattern covers them by reading.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/lint': minor`, `'@objectstack/spec': patch`. One moved package at `minor` discharges `narrowed` (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs:907-910`, `:1886-1887`). No `major`. Correct.
- The BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO section and the `adr-0087: registered` marker are unchanged and still present.
- The ADR-0087 entry is unchanged in the delta. It agrees with `narrowed`: it states seven publish refusals of metadata that was accepted before, as a notice with no conversion. Nothing in it says the protocol is unchanged. It does not mention the blank-name arm; that arm is the same rule id and the same remedy, so no edit is owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **S2 closed.** `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx:3032` and `:3097` carry `timezone: 'UTC'`. Both spec docblocks carry it (`time-relative-trigger.zod.ts:44`, `schedule-organization.zod.ts:122`). The two reference pages carry the same line, character for character, as their source docblock. No other reference page changed, and no other docblock was touched, so no page is stale.
